t:
(a) Tribal Claims.—The benefits realized by the Tribe under this subtitle shall be in complete replacement of, complete substitution for, and full satisfaction of all—
        (1) claims of the Tribe against the United States waived and released pursuant to section 3720(a); and 
        (2) objections withdrawn pursuant to section 3720(c).  
    (b) Allottee Claims.—The benefits realized by the allottees under this subtitle shall be in complete replacement of, complete substitution for, and full satisfaction of—
        (1) all claims waived and released pursuant to section 3720(a)(2); and 
        (2) any claim of an allottee against the United States similar in nature to a claim described in section 3720(a)(2) that the allottee asserted or could have asserted.

fable.w: The tempting reading is that mentioning a Tribe, allottees, and claims or objections against the United States signals outside-party involvement or a right to sue. But the section only says settlement benefits fully satisfy claims already waived and objections already withdrawn. It extinguishes claims rather than granting any right to sue, and it sets up no consultation, hearing, comment, or advisory process before a federal decision.
fable.s: The benefits realized by the Tribe under this subtitle shall be in complete replacement of, complete substitution for, and full satisfaction of all

opus.w: This is a settlement provision. It treats the Tribe's and allottees' claims against the United States as fully satisfied and their objections as withdrawn. It is tempting to call this participation because outside parties' claims and objections appear, but the section takes away rights to sue or object rather than granting them. It also creates no process for outside parties to take part in a future federal decision.
opus.s: The benefits realized by the Tribe under this subtitle shall be in complete replacement of, complete substitution for, and full satisfaction of all—
opus.b: 1. **Tempting reading:** The section mentions a tribe's and allottees' "claims against the United States" and "objections withdrawn." Since tribes and allottees are outside the federal government, it might look like a right to sue or object. That reading fails. The section does not give anyone a right to sue or object. It says the settlement benefits fully replace and satisfy claims that have been waived and objections that have been withdrawn, so it ends outside parties' legal challenges. It also sets up no consultation, hearing, comment period or advisory body before a federal decision.

qwen_chat.w: This section defines the legal scope of a settlement, stating that benefits replace and satisfy previously waived claims and withdrawn objections. It does not establish a mechanism for outside parties to consult with, advise, or participate in federal decision-making. The reference to 'objections withdrawn' describes the status of past claims, not a current requirement for public participation or consultation.
qwen_chat.s: The benefits realized by the Tribe under this subtitle shall be in complete replacement of, complete substitution for, and full satisfaction of all— (1) claims of the Tribe against the United States waived and released pursuant to section 3720(a); and (2) objections withdrawn pursuant to section 3720(c).
qwen_chat.b: Tempting-but-wrong reading: One might argue that "objections withdrawn" implies a process where the Tribe or allottees participated in raising objections, thus constituting participation. However, the text here is purely about the legal effect of the settlement (releasing claims), not about a procedural requirement for outside parties to consult with the government before a decision is made. The "objections" referenced are likely part of a past legislative or administrative process, and this section merely defines the scope of the release. There is no requirement for current or future consultation, comment periods, or advisory roles involving non-federal parties in the decision-making process described here.
